title: Coherent reduction of normalized ordinary tensor reindexing
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, and let $g:X\xrightarrow\sim Y$ be an isomorphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible. Use the recorded coherent coefficient calculus [def-coef-derived-system-calculus-data]. Put $F=$ ordinary reindexing, $R_W=$ coherent reduction and $L_W=$ total derived limit. Let $A$ be normalized completion reindexing data [def-pod-completion-reindex-models], with reduction isomorphism $a:P R_Y\cong R_X F$, where $P$ is the whole-system inverse image. Let $c$ be ordinary tensor/Hom comparison data [def-pod-reindexing-coherence-data], and let $h$ identify its derived functor with $F$ by equality. Write $\mu:F(M\otimes_Y N)	o FM\otimes_X FN$ for the tensor map transported along $h$, $b_W$ for reductionTensor and $
u$ for the canonical system tensor comparison [def-pur-completed-pullback-tower-realizations], transported along the proved equality of the two presentations of $P$. Then for arbitrary ambient derived $M,N$ on $Y$ one has $P(b_Y);
u_{R_YM,R_YN};(a_M\otimes a_N)=a_{M\otimes N};R_X(\mu);b_X$. The equation is in the whole system category and contains no completion, total limit, augmentation or constructibility condition. The same module constructs the equality-transported comparison $
u$ without choosing new data.

proof.text: Take simultaneous flat-term K-flat representatives and use the recorded integral and reduction tensor model squares. Transport c.tensor to ordinary reindexing by h. The equality of the sequence pullback presentations transports the canonical system tensor comparison without choosing any new morphism.

The proved podReindexing_reduction_inv_mate identity identifies A.reduction inverse as the whole-system adjunct of the reindexed unit followed by A.limit. LimitModel computes this adjunct from the actual strict Roos map, so this does not infer equality from finite derived evaluations. The ordinary quotient units, FiniteModel and QuotientGenerators identify the strict reduction comparisons with A.quotient. Use c.tensorChain_pure: on each homogeneous pure tensor the two strict composites send b tensor (x tensor y) to the same pair of reduced reindexed factors. QuotientTransition gives compatibility with every system transition. Tensor generators and total-summand injections identify entire system chain maps, and product K-flat localization descends the equality. The calculation includes zero inputs and empty schemes, and requires no Tor bound or completeness.

theorem podReindexing_reduction_tensor_square
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso g]
    [∀ x : X, Invertible (l : X.residueField x)]
    [∀ y : Y, Invertible (l : Y.residueField y)]
    (A : PodCompletionReindex l E g) (hA : PodCompletionReindex.Laws l E g A)
    (c : PodReindexingCoherence.Comparison l E g none
      (podReindexCalculus l E X).integralClosed (podReindexCalculus l E Y).integralClosed
      (podReindexCalculus l E X).integralTensorModel
      (podReindexCalculus l E Y).integralTensorModel)
    (h : podReindexingDerivedFunctor l E g none = podOrdinaryReindex l E g)
    (M N : podReindexingDerived l E Y none) :
    let q := podReindexingTensorFrame l E g A hA M N
    let v : q.F.obj q.S ⟶ q.T := podReindexingIntegralTensorHom l E g c h M N
    q.P.map q.bY ≫ q.w₁ ≫ q.w₂ = q.a ≫ q.LX.map v ≫ q.bX
